messages:
Julia (support): heads up — AcmeOps opened a ticket about intermittent 429s since ~02:00 UTC. They report low steady traffic but short intense fanouts. Can we triage?

AcmeOps: yes, we ran a nightly export at 02:00 that fans out to ~200 worker processes. avg ~100 rpm, but bursts to ~2000 reqs/sec for ~5-10s. Clients get 429s with retry-after ~3s.

Omar (oncall): can you paste an example response (headers + body) and the API key id? also which region/endpoint?

AcmeOps: sending sample below. key: acct-ACME-01 region: us-west-2

AcmeOps (paste):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit-RPM: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining-RPM: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset-RPM: 38
X-RateLimit-Limit-TPM: 36000
X-RateLimit-Remaining-TPM: 35400
Retry-After: 3
{ "error": "rate_limited", "message": "RPM limit exceeded" }
```

Mira (sre): header pattern looks like per-minute (RPM) bucket hit. Remaining-TPM still OK so total minute budget not exhausted. This is classic short high-concurrency fanout causing the short-window RPM cap to be exceeded.

Mira (sre): quick checks: 1) Are worker processes using the same API key concurrently? 2) Do they retry aggressively (no jitter)? 3) Any client-side batching that could be collapsed?

AcmeOps: yes, all workers share a single key and our retry is exponential but with small base and no jitter. We launch jobs in parallel when cron triggers.

Lee (support): short-term mitigation options: 1) ask client to stagger the fanout (add jitter/splay) 2) set client concurrency cap to keep instantaneous rpm under limit 3) enable per-key burst allowance (if we can apply) 4) request a temporary RPM uplift from infra for next 30m.

Mira (sre): I can temporarily increase their RPM carveout from 600 -> 3000 for 30 minutes while they deploy a fix. Need account owner + sales approval. If approved I can patch rate-limiter config and monitor.

Omar (oncall): can we confirm there were no infra regressions? @sre-bot, any deploys to rate-limiter or edge recently?

sre-bot: deploy event: service: rate-limiter, env: prod, release: v2.3.8, start: 2025-11-01T01:12:00Z, completed: 01:15:23Z. No errors.

Mira (sre): deploy time doesn't line up with spikes. Looks client-triggered.

Lee (support): @AcmeOps we recommend these immediate changes (quick checklist):
- Add randomized jitter to worker start times (uniform +/- 30s)
- Limit concurrency per process to N so aggregate rpm < 600 (suggest start with 200 rpm per process)
- Apply exponential backoff with full jitter for retries (eg, base 100ms, max 5s)
- If you need a fast fix: approve temporary RPM uplift and we will apply a 30m carveout.

AcmeOps: can you apply the uplift while we roll out jitter? yes please, if you can do 30m bump that buys time.

Julia (support): recorded: customer approved. Asking for uplift: 600->3000 RPM for 30m.

Mira (sre): applying config change now. Patch command: `rlctl set-acct-cap --acct acct-ACME-01 --rpm 3000 --ttl 1800` (internal tool). Will watch slow metrics.

Mira (sre): patched. Observing 5m windows: error rate down from 12% -> 0.8% during next scheduled run.

AcmeOps: confirming on our side — retries reduced and exports mostly succeed. We'll push jitter in next deploy (ETA 45m).

Omar (oncall): follow-up items (short):
- Support to schedule a permanent RPM increase or guidance on partitioning keys if they need concurrent fanouts.
- Product: consider adding a "burst-safe" client guide for customers doing large fanouts.
- SRE: add a monitoring alert to surface RPM-saturated keys (not just overall 429) so we can catch these earlier.

Lee (support): I'll open the account uplift ticket with Sales for formal approval if they want a permanent bump.

Mira (sre): closing immediate on-call loop; re-open if error rate climbs.

AcmeOps: thanks everyone, will report back after the jitter deploy. :thumbsup:
